arxiv-1912-07952.title: Breathing Modes, Quartic Nonlinearities and Effective Resonant Systems
arxiv-1912-07952.creator: Oleg EVNIN †‡
arxiv-1912-07952.description: Abstract A breathing mode in a Hamiltonian system is a function on the phase space whose evolution is exactly periodic for all solutions of the equations of motion. Such breathing modes are familiar from nonlinear dynamics in harmonic traps or anti-de Sitter spacetimes, with applications to the physics of cold atomic gases, general relativity and high-energy physics.

arxiv-2109-08365.title: CodeQA: A Question Answering Dataset for Source Code Comprehension
arxiv-2109-08365.creator: Chenxiao Liu, Xiaojun Wan
arxiv-2109-08365.description: Abstract We propose CodeQA, a free-form question answering dataset for the purpose of source code comprehension: given a code snippet and a question, a textual answer is required to be generated. CodeQA contains a Java dataset with 119,778 question-answer pairs and a Python dataset with 70,085 question-answer pairs.

arxiv-2110-08819.title: Geometric approach to Lieb-Schultz-Mattis theorem without translation symmetry under inversion or rotation symmetry
arxiv-2110-08819.creator: Yuan Yao, Akira Furusaki
arxiv-2110-08819.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yuan Yao, Akira Furusaki. We propose a geometric approach to Lieb-Schultz-Mattis theorem for quantum many-body systems with discrete spin-rotation symmetries and lattice inversion or rotation symmetry, but without translation symmetry assumed. Under symmetry-twisting on a ( d − 1 ) (d-1) -dimensional plane, we find that any d d -dimensional inversion-symmetric spin system possesses a doubly degenerate spectrum when it hosts a half-integer spin at the inversion-symmetric point.

arxiv-2112-02132.title: Optimal Vehicle Path Planning Using Quadratic Optimization for Baidu Apollo Open Platform
arxiv-2112-02132.creator: Yajia Zhang*, Hongyi Sun, Jinyun Zhou, Jiacheng Pan, Jiangtao Hu, Jinghao Miao
arxiv-2112-02132.description: Abstract Path planning is a key component in motion planning for autonomous vehicles. A path specifies the geometrical shape that the vehicle will travel, thus, it is critical to safe and comfortable vehicle motions. For urban driving scenarios, autonomous vehicles need the ability to navigate in cluttered environment, e.g., roads partially blocked by a number of vehicles/obstacles on the sides.

arxiv-2112-10805.title: SDSS-IV MaNGA: Cannibalism Caught in the Act – on the Frequency of Occurrence of Multiple Cores in Brightest Cluster Galaxies Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2112-10805.creator: Yun-Hsin Hsu (徐允心), Yen-Ting Lin, Song Huang, Dylan Nelson, Vicente Rodriguez-Gomez, Hsuan-Ting Lai, Jenny Greene, Alexie Leauthaud, Alfonso Aragón-Salamanca, Kevin Bundy, Eric Emsellem, Michael Merrifield, Surhud More, Nobuhiro Okabe, Yu Rong, Joel R. Brownstein, Richard R. Lane, Kaike Pan, Donald
arxiv-2112-10805.description: Abstract Although it is generally accepted that massive galaxies form in a two-phased fashion, beginning with a rapid mass buildup through intense starburst activities, followed by primarily dry mergers that mainly deposit stellar mass at outskirts, the late time stellar mass growth of brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs), the most massive galaxies in the universe, is still not well understood.

arxiv-2306-17801.title: Safe, Seamless, And Scalable Integration Of Asynchronous GPU Streams In PETSc
arxiv-2306-17801.creator: Jacob Faibussowitsch 1 , Mark F. Adams 2 , Richard Tran Mills 1 , Stefano Zampini 3 , Junchao Zhang 1
arxiv-2306-17801.description: Abstract Leveraging Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) to accelerate scientific software has proven to be highly successful, but in order to extract more performance, GPU programmers must overcome the high latency costs associated with their use. One method of reducing or hiding this latency cost is to use asynchronous streams to issue commands to the GPU.

arxiv-2410-00744.title: Topology of black hole phase transition in JT gravity Thanks: E-mail: dibakar.roychowdhury@ph.iitr.ac.in
arxiv-2410-00744.creator: Hemant Rathi
arxiv-2410-00744.description: Abstract We present a JT gravity setup coupled with U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) and S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) SU(2) Yang-Mills fields in two dimensions that reveals the onset of a small black hole to large black hole phase transition at finite chemical potential(s).

arxiv-2411-00749.title: PathoGen-X: A Cross-Modal Genomic Feature Trans-Align Network for Enhanced Survival Prediction from Histopathology Images
arxiv-2411-00749.creator: Akhila Krishna 1 Nikhil Cherian Kurian 2 Abhijeet Patil 1 Amruta Parulekar 1 Amit Sethi 1
arxiv-2411-00749.description: Abstract Accurate survival prediction is essential for personalized cancer treatment. However, genomic data – often a more powerful predictor than pathology data – is costly and inaccessible. We present the cross-modal genomic feature translation and alignment network for enhanced survival prediction from histopathology images (PathoGen-X).

arxiv-2412-00180.title: Strong Constraints on Dark Photon and Scalar Dark Matter Decay from INTEGRAL and AMS-02
arxiv-2412-00180.creator: Thong T.Q. Nguyen, Isabelle John, Tim Linden, Tim M.P. Tait
arxiv-2412-00180.description: Abstract We investigate the decay of bosonic dark matter with masses between 1 MeV and 2 TeV into Standard Model final states. We specifically focus on dark photons that kinetically mix with the Standard Model, as well as scalar dark matter models that have Yukawa couplings with the Standard Model.

arxiv-2504-00294.title: Inference-Time Scaling for Complex Tasks: Where We Stand and What Lies Ahead
arxiv-2504-00294.creator: Vidhisha Balachandran, Jingya Chen, Lingjiao Chen, Shivam Garg, Neel Joshi, Yash Lara, John Langford, Besmira Nushi, Vibhav Vineet, Yue Wu, Safoora Yousefi
arxiv-2504-00294.description: Abstract Inference-time scaling can enhance the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) on complex problems that benefit from step-by-step problem solving. Although lengthening generated scratchpads has proven effective for mathematical tasks, the broader impact of this approach on other tasks remains less clear.

arxiv-2510-09805.title: Temporal Lifting as Latent-Space Regularization for Continuous-Time Flow Models in AI Systems
arxiv-2510-09805.creator: Jeffrey Camlin
arxiv-2510-09805.description: Abstract We present a latent-space formulation of adaptive temporal reparametrization for continuous-time dynamical systems. The method, called temporal lifting , introduces a smooth monotone mapping t ↦ τ ⁡ ( t ) t\mapsto\tau(t) that regularizes near-singular behavior of the underlying flow while preserving its conservation laws.

arxiv-2510-22464.title: Robust Spatial Confounding Adjustment via Basis Voting
arxiv-2510-22464.creator: Anik Burman, Elizabeth L. Ogburn, Abhirup Datta Department of Biostatistics, Johns Hopkins University
arxiv-2510-22464.description: Abstract Estimating causal effects of spatially structured exposures is complicated by unmeasured spatial confounders, which undermine identifiability in spatial linear regression models unless structural assumptions are imposed. We develop a general framework for causal effect estimation that relaxes the commonly assumed requirement that exposures contain higher-frequency variation than confounders.

arxiv-2512-08303.title: Quantum-classical correspondence in resonant and nonresonant Rabi-Stark model
arxiv-2512-08303.creator: Shangyun Wang 1 , Songbai Chen 2,3 , Jiliang Jing 2,3
arxiv-2512-08303.description: Abstract Abstract Testing the correspondence principle in nonlinear quantum systems is a fundamental pursuit in quantum physics. In this paper, we employed mean field approximation theory to study the semiclassical dynamics in the Rabi-Stark model (RSM) and showed that the nonlinear Stark coupling significantly modulates the semiclassical phase space structure.

arxiv-2601-05219.title: CAOS: Conformal Aggregation of One-Shot Predictors
arxiv-2601-05219.creator: Maja Waldron
arxiv-2601-05219.description: Abstract One-shot prediction enables rapid adaptation of pretrained foundation models to new tasks using only one labeled example, but lacks principled uncertainty quantification. While conformal prediction provides finite-sample coverage guarantees, standard split conformal methods are inefficient in the one-shot setting due to data splitting and reliance on a single predictor.

pmc-11460506.title: An inhibitory acetylcholine receptor gates context-dependent mechanosensory processing in C. elegans
pmc-11460506.creator: Sandeep Kumar, Anuj K. Sharma, Andrew M. Leifer
pmc-11460506.description: SummaryAn animal’s current behavior influences its response to sensory stimuli, but the molecular and circuit-level mechanisms of this context-dependent decision-making are not well understood. Caenorhabditis elegans are less likely to respond to a mechanosensory stimulus by reversing if the stimuli is received while the animal turns. Inhibitory feedback from turning associated neurons are needed for this gating.

pmc-11714838.title: Cumulative Incidence Rate Score for Alzheimer’s Disease Risk is Associated with White Matter Hyperintensity Volume in Older Adults Without Dementia
pmc-11714838.creator: Rafael V Lippert, Natalie C Edwards, Giuseppe Tosto, Jeffrey D Pyne, Patrick J Lao, Adam M Brickman
pmc-11714838.description: BackgroundSmall vessel cerebrovascular disease (CVD), visualized as white matter hyperintensities (WMH) on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), is associated with risk and progression of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) in clinical, community, and genetic studies of AD. However, it is unclear whether these observations indicate a role of CVD in AD pathogenesis.

pmc-12490087.title: Detection of AcrAB efflux pump mediated ciprofloxacin resistance in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae in Nepal
pmc-12490087.creator: Sadikshya Kharel, Sandesh Rimal, Babita Neupane, Bijay Kumar Sharma, Narayan Sharma Bashyal, Yogendra Shah, Bimal Sharma Chalise, Manisha Rawal, Mya Myat Ngwe Tun, Shyam Prakash Dumre
pmc-12490087.description: BackgroundAntimicrobial resistance (AMR) has emerged as a serious public health threat with a sharply increasing burden globally. Resource limited countries like Nepal are facing difficulties in the fight against AMR. This has been further worsened due to the lack of adequate molecular data.

pmc-12565369.title: Innate Immunity in the Pathogenesis of Selected Autoimmune Neurological Diseases
pmc-12565369.creator: Julia Rudnicka-Czerwiec, Halina Bartosik-Psujek, Laureline Berthelot
pmc-12565369.description: The human immune system consists of two main components: innate and adaptive immunity. To date, research on the pathogenesis of autoimmune neurological diseases has primarily focused on the role of adaptive immunity. However, growing evidence highlights the significant contribution of innate immune mechanisms in the development of neurological disorders.

pmc-12802776.title: The facilitators and barriers to home-based robotic rehabilitation in India: a pilot feasibility study
pmc-12802776.creator: Aravind Nehrujee, A. T. Prabhakar, Sathish Balaraman, Rasika Bombatkar, Henry Prakash, Selvaraj Samuelkamaleshkumar, Sanjith Aaron, Suranjan Bhattacharji, S. Sujatha, Sivakumar Balasubramanian
pmc-12802776.description: IntroductionRobot-assisted rehabilitation has emerged as a promising approach for enhancing motor function in stroke survivors. However, the feasibility and effectiveness of home-based robotic training in this population are underexplored, especially in low/middle-income countries.MethodsThis feasibility study aimed to address this gap by examining the feasibility and effectiveness of independent home-based training using PLUTO, a robotic device for hand training.

pmc-13184567.title: Polypropylene wiping cloths contaminated with S. aureus and P. aeruginosa transfer significantly less to uncontaminated surfaces compared to microfiber and cotton
pmc-13184567.creator: Maxwell Voorn, Geraldine Tembo, Siddharth Kumar, Haley Oliver-Jischke, Peter Teska
pmc-13184567.description: Background:Cross-contamination from contaminated wiping cloths is an underrecognized route of pathogen transmission in healthcare settings. Reused, misapplied, or ineffective disinfectants can transfer viable bacteria between surfaces. Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa persist under hospital conditions and are frequently isolated in healthcare environments.
